chapter: Teaching programs, mentors, White House and other bands
title: A short stint with Lionel Hampton
summary: Baker played only two weeks and part of a tour with Hampton in the mid-1950s because the pay was bad and the personnel constantly changed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I’d like to go back and pick up some things in your career that we moved away from as we were doing the chronology of your performing career. I think we talked a little bit about your time with Lionel Hampton, but this might be a good time, now that we’re talking about Lionel Hampton, to go back there and pick that up.

I didn’t spend a lot of time with Lionel Hampton. I worked in the summers, two weeks one summer and a part of a tour a second summer, because, first of all, the money was really dreadful. I think you made some ridiculous – he had no per diem, and

he didn’t pay for the rooms. And even though I was still in college, I knew that something was wrong. So I didn’t spend a lot of time with him, nor did I really treasure my moments there. It was a chance to meet people like Jimmy Cleveland and the rest of them, with . . .
About what year – what time would that have been?
This would have been in the mid-’50s, because I went out in the summertime when school was not in session, you know, 'cause he was always – the personnel changed as rapidly as the weather.
He didn’t have a wonderful reputation about taking care of the people in the band.
